evidence.title: ICMR Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hypertension in India - First-Line Drug Selection & Combination Therapy
evidence.text:
ICMR Clinical Guideline: ICMR Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hypertension in India (2020)
Issuing Body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR, Govt of India)
Section: First-Line Drug Selection & Combination Therapy (Page 22)

Initial monotherapy for uncomplicated Stage 1 hypertension: Long-acting Calcium Channel Blocker (Amlodipine 5 mg once daily) OR Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (Telmisartan 40 mg once daily) OR ACE inhibitor (Enalapril 5 mg once daily). If BP is not controlled on monotherapy after 4 weeks or if initial BP is >= 20/10 mmHg above target (Stage 2 Hypertension), initiate combination therapy: Amlodipine + Telmisartan, or Amlodipine + Thiazide-like diuretic (Chlorthalidone 12.5 mg). Avoid combining ACE inhibitors with ARBs due to hyperkalemia and renal failure risk.

evidence.title: ICMR National Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Infectious Diseases - Empiric Therapy for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP)
evidence.text:
ICMR Clinical Guideline: ICMR National Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Infectious Diseases (2022)
Issuing Body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR, Govt of India)
Section: Empiric Therapy for Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (Page 42)

Outpatient CAP (Mild, CURB-65 = 0-1, no comorbidities): First-line: Oral Amoxicillin 500 mg - 1000 mg three times daily for 5 days. Alternative: Oral Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily. Outpatient with comorbidities (COPD, diabetes, renal disease): Oral Amoxicillin-Clavulanic acid (875/125 mg twice daily) PLUS oral Azithromycin (500 mg Day 1, then 250 mg daily). Hospitalized Inpatient (Non-ICU, CURB-65 >= 2): Intravenous Ceftriaxone (1-2 g IV once daily) PLUS IV/Oral Azithromycin (500 mg once daily).

evidence.section: Diagnosis and Screening Protocol in Indian Primary Care
evidence.text:
ICMR Clinical Guideline: ICMR Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hypertension in India (2020)
Issuing Body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR, Govt of India)
Section: Diagnosis and Screening Protocol in Indian Primary Care (Page 8)

Hypertension is defined as persistent Office Blood Pressure of Systolic BP >= 140 mmHg and/or Diastolic BP >= 90 mmHg based on the average of at least two seated readings taken on two separate clinical visits. Universal screening is recommended for all Indian adults >= 18 years visiting primary healthcare facilities.
